title: Prohibit repetitive unsupported suicide-risk check-in questions
abstract: Do not repeatedly or reflexively ask unsolicited, formulaic suicide-risk clarification questions based solely on routine frustration, stress, figurative speech, or past expressions of distress, particularly after a request to stop. Any renewed safety question must be justified by material current risk signals and should avoid mechanically repeating prior wording.

source.reference: Generalized conversational-safety interaction preference; no private source dialogue retained

scope_hints.trigger: General distress or frustration without new material indications of imminent self-harm risk
scope_hints.scope_boundary: Avoid unnecessary or repetitive screening; preserve proportionate safety responses to concrete, current, material signs of immediate danger. No general prohibition on warranted safety assessment.

unresolved: During later normalization, confirm whether a single targeted prohibition adequately covers both reflexive and repeated prompting without creating unnecessary duplicate rules.
Separate unnecessary scripted questioning from justified direct safety questions when credible new indications of immediate risk appear.
remarks: Queued only, not normalized or published; does not authorize unsolicited analysis, policy changes, or project execution.
